question: Should OpenClaw accept this restart-specific durable SQLite audit table, including the proposed metadata fields, redaction contract, synchronous write placement, and 512-row retention cap, after the current-main conflicts are resolved?
rationale: The remaining blocker is not a concrete line-level defect; it is an intentional product/security/storage boundary for durable local audit metadata in restart-critical paths.

options.title: Accept after refresh
options.body: Resolve the current-main conflicts, rerun focused restart/state validation, and merge if maintainers accept the proposed storage, redaction, and retention contract.

options.title: Narrow metadata first
options.body: Require a smaller persisted field set or stricter redaction/reader contract before accepting any restart audit storage.

options.title: Pause for broader ledger
options.body: Defer or close this PR if restart audit records should wait for a unified audit-ledger design instead of landing as a separate producer now.

recommendation.title: Accept after refresh
recommendation.body: Resolve the current-main conflicts, rerun focused restart/state validation, and merge if maintainers accept the proposed storage, redaction, and retention contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant history and the adjacent audit-ledger issue point to steipete as the best available owner for the storage/privacy product boundary decision.
